requirement: The system shall provide a Docker Compose environment for local development and testing that starts Airflow, Postgres, a standalone Spark master, Spark workers, and Jupyter/PySpark services together. Airflow shall use Postgres to persist its scheduler metadata.

Users shall be able to access the Airflow, Spark master, Jupyter, and Spark application web interfaces from the host machine. The deployment shall provide configured host port mappings for these services, the Spark cluster connection, and Postgres.

The environment shall share DAG definitions, Spark application files, notebooks, and input data with the containers that need them, so scheduled jobs and interactive notebooks can access their required files. Jupyter notebooks shall be stored in the mounted notebook directory.

Airflow shall load DAG definitions from the mounted DAG directory and make them available for manual triggering or scheduling. Spark jobs shall be submitted to the deployed standalone Spark cluster using SparkSubmitOperator and the configured spark_default connection. The Airflow environment shall include PySpark to support Spark submission.

Spark workers shall register with the master and execute assigned workloads using their configured memory and CPU resources. Operators shall be able to increase the worker count by adding worker services using the existing configuration pattern.
Users shall be able to access Jupyter with its access token and run interactive PySpark notebooks using the shared notebook and data directories.

Users shall be able to inspect submitted Spark applications and their execution state through the Spark master web interface, review task output in Airflow logs, and inspect container logs for operational information.

The packaged Spark runtime shall remain compatible with Spark 2.4.5 built for Hadoop 2.6. The Airflow-side Python environment shall retain the declared dependency version pins and include PySpark to support reproducible operation.
